newsitem.title: USA: Brooksley Born sworn in as CFTC chief.
newsitem.headline: Brooksley Born sworn in as CFTC chief.

text.p: Brooksley Born, a commodities expert and lawyer, was sworn in Monday as the seventh chairperson of the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal agency regulating U.S. futures markets.
The CFTC said Born's oath of office was administered by Acting Chairman John Tull at the agency's headquarters here, attended by senior agency officials.
Born was nominated by President Clinton on May 3 and confirmed by the Senate on August 2. Her term expires on April 15, 1999.
Another commissioner confirmed by the Senate, David Spears, a former aide to Republican presidential candidate Robert Dole, is expected to be sworn in next week.
Born was a partner at the law firm of Arnold & Porter, before assuming the CFTC post.

Senate confirmation of her nomination was snagged for some time due to objections by Sen. Lauch Faircloth, a North Carolina Republican, who raised the issue of Born's reported close friendship with the first lady, Hillary Rodham Clinton.
Faircloth contended that such a relationship might create a conflict of interest if in the future the CFTC were called upon to look into Mrs. Clinton's commodities trading in the late 1970s.
He withdrew his objections after Born wrote a letter saying she wold recuse herself from any possible investigation involving Mrs. Clinton's commodities trading.
